frameworks.name: verl (Volcengine)
frameworks.bestFor: Production-grade distributed RL (PPO, GRPO, GSPO, DAPO) & On-Policy Distillation with flexible hybrid GPU placement.
frameworks.hardware: NVIDIA, AMD/ROCm, Ascend; single-node multi-GPU up to multi-node clusters. Trainer and rollout sampler share/swap GPUs dynamically.
frameworks.multiStep: Yes — AgentLoops support multi-turn tool-calling rollouts.
frameworks.rubricJudge: Yes — custom or generative reward functions return rubric scores.
frameworks.rlAlgorithms: PPO, GRPO, GSPO, DAPO, RLOO, REINFORCE++
frameworks.sweetSpot: Midsize teams (8B–35B+) scaling from 4–8 GPUs to clusters; widely adopted reference architecture for asynchronous hybrid throughput.

frameworks.name: SkyRL (UC Berkeley / Anyscale)
frameworks.bestFor: Asynchronous multi-turn agentic RL for enterprise workloads (proven in production by Coinbase Fraud Agent & Mercor APEX-Agents).
frameworks.hardware: 1× high-VRAM GPU (e.g. RTX PRO 6000 96GB / H100) up to multi-node H200 clusters on Ray/Anyscale.
frameworks.multiStep: Yes — native multi-turn containerized & tool-calling environments (Harbor integration).
frameworks.rubricJudge: Yes — supports programmatic verifiers and LLM rubric judges.
frameworks.rlAlgorithms: GRPO, DAPO, CISPO, async off-policy stabilized RL
frameworks.sweetSpot: Enterprise teams already on Ray/vLLM wanting battle-tested multi-turn agentic RL recipes.

frameworks.name: PrimeRL + Prime Verifiers
frameworks.bestFor: Clean separation of RL environments/evals (Verifiers) and scalable async FSDP2 + vLLM training (PrimeRL) with OPD.
frameworks.hardware: RTX 3090/4090/5090, A100, H100, B200; 4B LoRA runs on 1× H100; scales cleanly to multi-node clusters.
frameworks.multiStep: Yes — Verifiers environments natively model multi-turn tool interactions.
frameworks.rubricJudge: Yes — built-in JudgeRubric with custom prompts and composable reward weights.
frameworks.rlAlgorithms: Async RL (GRPO/CISPO family) via PrimeRL; legacy Verifiers trainers deprecated.
frameworks.distillation: SFT + native On-Policy Distillation (OPD) in PrimeRL.
frameworks.sweetSpot: Teams building reusable evaluation environments first and plugging into clean async RL/OPD.

frameworks.name: OpenPipe ART
frameworks.bestFor: Lightweight multi-turn agentic GRPO framework (validated on Qwen2.5-14B single-H100 runs).
frameworks.hardware: 1× NVIDIA GPU (co-located Unsloth/torchtune + vLLM alternating) or separated GPUs via PipelineTrainer or W&B Serverless.
frameworks.multiStep: Yes — arbitrary Python agent loops with multiple LLM & MCP tool calls, plus Additional Histories support.
frameworks.rubricJudge: Yes — built-in RULER relative trajectory judge plus custom reward/rubric hooks.
frameworks.sweetSpot: Small teams (1–4 GPUs) prototyping vertical agents (email, SQL, CRM, MCP tools) in days.

frameworks.name: Unsloth
frameworks.bestFor: Ultra-memory-efficient LoRA/QLoRA SFT and single-GPU RL (GRPO, GSPO, DAPO) with chunked logit/loss kernels.
frameworks.hardware: NVIDIA, AMD, Intel; shares base weights between trainer and vLLM sampler on the same GPU (~5 GB VRAM for 1.5B RL).
frameworks.multiStep: Yes — acts as the memory-optimized training backend underneath OpenPipe ART.
frameworks.rubricJudge: Yes — custom Python reward functions (or RULER via ART).
frameworks.distillation: SFT on teacher traces (no standalone OPD trainer documented yet).
frameworks.sweetSpot: Single-GPU workstation / 1× H100 experimentation, fast LoRA SFT, and low-budget 1.5B–14B RL.

frameworks.name: Hugging Face TRL
frameworks.bestFor: Standard, well-documented all-in-one PyTorch library for SFT, DPO, multi-turn GRPO, RLOO, and On-Policy Distillation.
frameworks.hardware: Single GPU to multi-node via Accelerate/FSDP/DeepSpeed; Liger fused kernels (`use_liger_kernel=True`) slash logit VRAM.
frameworks.multiStep: Yes — GRPOTrainer now supports stateful multi-turn environments and custom rollout functions.
frameworks.rubricJudge: Yes — pluggable Python reward callables and judge endpoints.
frameworks.rlAlgorithms: SFT, DPO, KTO, ORPO, GRPO, RLOO, AsyncGRPOTrainer
frameworks.sweetSpot: Standard enterprise ML teams wanting long-term Hugging Face ecosystem compatibility and clean abstractions.

frameworks.name: Tinker (Thinking Machines API)
frameworks.bestFor: Training-as-a-Service API exposing low-level SFT, RL, Rubric Grading, and OPD primitives without managing GPU clusters.
frameworks.hardware: Zero local GPU ops — your agent loop & eval logic run locally while Tinker executes distributed forward/backward/sampling remotely.
frameworks.multiStep: Yes — client-side agent loop with rich cookbook recipes.
frameworks.rubricJudge: Yes — first-class Rubric Grading cookbook recipes.
frameworks.rlAlgorithms: Custom policy gradients, GRPO, CISPO via API primitives
frameworks.sweetSpot: Teams that want full algorithmic control (including OPD & custom RL) without hiring GPU infrastructure engineers.

frameworks.name: OpenRLHF
frameworks.bestFor: Mature Ray + vLLM distributed RLHF and multi-turn agent training with classic and modern policy gradient algorithms.
frameworks.hardware: NVIDIA/CUDA multi-GPU and multi-node Ray clusters with DeepSpeed ZeRO & vLLM.
frameworks.rubricJudge: Yes — custom reward functions and external reward servers.
frameworks.distillation: Teacher SFT supported; no dedicated built-in OPD trainer.
frameworks.sweetSpot: Teams wanting mature PPO/REINFORCE++ baselines on Ray clusters.

frameworks.name: rLLM (Agentica)
frameworks.bestFor: Long-horizon software engineering and reasoning agents (powered Together × Agentica DeepSWE-32B).
frameworks.hardware: Multi-GPU to 64× H100 clusters for full 32B SWE runs; lighter setups with LoRA or Tinker backend.
frameworks.multiStep: Yes — up to 100-step containerized SWE/tool trajectories.
frameworks.rubricJudge: Yes — environment unit-test verifiers or custom rubric rewards.
frameworks.distillation: SFT + OPD recipe with Tinker backend.
frameworks.sweetSpot: Coding agents, containerized execution environments, and long-horizon SWE RL.

frameworks.name: Microsoft Agent Lightning
frameworks.bestFor: Adding RL post-training to existing production agent frameworks (LangChain, AutoGen, OpenAI Agents SDK, ServiceNow) without code rewrites.
frameworks.hardware: Decoupled agent execution workers + GPU training backend (verl/vLLM compatible).
frameworks.multiStep: Yes — traces arbitrary multi-agent and multi-turn production executions.
frameworks.rlAlgorithms: GRPO / hierarchical multi-agent RL via pluggable trainers
frameworks.distillation: Trajectory collection supports SFT / imitation pipelines.
frameworks.sweetSpot: Enterprises with existing agent orchestrators who refuse to rewrite their business logic for an RL library.

frameworks.name: Scale AI AgentEnv
frameworks.bestFor: Standardized multi-turn enterprise agent environment framework for evaluation and RL rollouts.
frameworks.hardware: Containerized sandbox infrastructure decoupled from trainer choice.
frameworks.multiStep: Yes — built specifically for stateful multi-step agent environments.
frameworks.rubricJudge: Yes — structured verifier and rubric interfaces.
frameworks.rlAlgorithms: Environment layer (pairs with verl, SkyRL, PrimeRL, TRL)
frameworks.sweetSpot: Teams standardizing reproducible sandboxed environments across evals and RL.

hardwareSizing.rlHardware: 1× RTX 4090 / A10G (5–24 GB via Unsloth co-located vLLM)
hardwareSizing.servingProfile: Sub-30ms TTFT, >200–2,800 tok/s; ideal for routing, tagging, fast-context search, edge/on-device.

hardwareSizing.rlHardware: 1× H100 / RTX PRO 6000 96GB (Coinbase ran 9B SkyRL for <$100); 2–4× H100 for long context
hardwareSizing.servingProfile: 0.5–0.7s end-to-end latency; outperforms frontier baselines on bounded fraud, classification, orchestration, and tool calling.

hardwareSizing.sftHardware: 1–2× H100 (80 GB) with LoRA (BF16/FP8); 4–8× H100 for full FT
hardwareSizing.rlHardware: 1× H100 for 14B LoRA GRPO (ART·E); 2–8× H100 with FP8/vLLM kernels for 27B–32B long-context RL
hardwareSizing.servingProfile: High reasoning + strict schema adherence; powers clinical scribes, legal compaction, email & code agents.

hardwareSizing.rlHardware: 2–8× H100 (low rollout latency due to 3B active parameters per token)
hardwareSizing.servingProfile: Combines ~30B parameter capacity with ~3B active-parameter FLOPs per token; well-suited to multi-turn enterprise retrieval.
